title: Weingart
description: A song credit set like a forme of hand-set metal type: three lines of title on a flush-left margin, a process-red running time printed underneath, brass rule, a reversed slug, small text cascading down the right. Every line is a row of single sorts, and every line's first sort is locked to the margin. Push a line and it hinges there like a lever, a step at a time: the far letter drops first, then the middle tips, and only a long pull breaks the word into a full staircase. Every sort drops straight down, its own piece of lead, so a word keeps its shape while its baseline breaks, and the Swiss margin it starts from never moves. The sorts are solid and stay in contact the way real lead does: a line that comes down onto the next one shoves the letters it lands on a step, and that line bends to them from the margin and, past that knee, takes on the riser of the line that hit it, sort for sort, and so on down the forme, each sort seating with its own knock, left to right, until the run locks. No sort ever hangs more than its own body below the one before it, and every riser, type or brass, is a whole number of the rule's own face, so a full push ends as four parallel stairs of one pitch, the three title lines and the brass rule running from the margin down to the red, where its last piece, cut to the figure's measure, seats on the red's baseline as its own rule. Only the red, printed in its own run, crosses the black, and where they overprint the two inks make a third, darker one.
intent: After Wolfgang Weingart's Basel letterpress experiments and his stepped Typografische Monatsblätter covers (1972–73): Swiss order broken from inside the system, using the real constraints of a press, quantised steps, letterspacing and overprinting, to make new rhythm. https://neugraphic.com/weingart/weingart-text2.html
